verdict: 2017 Police Interceptor Utility (3.7L Ti-VCT V6, 6-speed auto, AWD). Engine/trans are fairly durable, but ex-police use means heavy idle hours (idle hours not shown on odometer; ~98k mi may equal 150k+ engine-miles), hard braking, curb strikes and abuse. Explorer-family has known PTU and water pump issues.
major_issues: Internal water pump (driven by timing chain) leaks coolant into oil; ~80-150k mi, $1,000-2,000+ (engine-out style labor on 3.5/3.7). Power transfer unit (PTU) failure/leak 60-120k mi, $800-1,500. Exhaust manifold/ cat issues; rear A/C and suspension wear; heavy idle wear on engine/alternator (police alternators/batteries); cut wiring and holes from removed light bars/equipment; frame/cooling lines. Transmission cooler/ trans hard shifts under abuse.
risk_reason: Ex-fleet/police history, unknown idle hours, AWD PTU and internal water pump are both common >$1,000 failures; as-is with kids budget of $1,000 is thin.
inspect_today: Check oil for milky/coolant contamination and coolant level/color; look for PTU leaks and listen for whine/clunk on turns; read idle hours if the cluster can show them; look for drilled holes/cut wiring from police gear; check scan for codes, trans shift quality and fluid color, brake/rotor condition, suspension bushings and tires for uneven wear, alternator output, A/C, and frame/curb damage.

verdict: 2015 F-150 2.7L EcoBoost twin-turbo V6 + 6R80. 2.7 is generally considered sturdier than the 3.5 EcoBoost, but at 192k miles, an as-is truck is well beyond typical comfortable range; turbos, carbon/valves, cooling and trans are all at risk.
major_issues: Oil pan seal leaks (2015-17); turbo/wastegate/actuator failure 120-200k mi $1,500-3,500; cam phaser/timing chain wear 150k+ $1,800-3,500; carbon buildup on direct injection; water pump/coolant leaks; ignition coils/plugs; 6R80 trans harsh shifts/valve body $1,000-3,000; rear axle/wheel bearings, front suspension wear; intake/ turbo hoses (boost leaks).
risk_reason: 192k miles on turbocharged DI engine and 6R80 trans; any turbo, timing or trans item exceeds budget; wear items (suspension, brakes, tires) add up too.
inspect_today: Cold start listening for timing rattle/chain whine; check oil level/condition and under pan for leaks; turbo shaft play/blue smoke on accel; boost hoses; scan for misfire/P0016-type codes; trans fluid color/smell and shift quality (flare, harsh 1-2/3-4); coolant leaks at water pump; look at frame rust, ball joints, tie rods, and rear axle seals.

verdict: 2018 Fiesta SE 1.6L Duratec. Engine is simple and reasonably durable, but if the car has the 6-speed automatic it is the PowerShift DPS6 dry dual-clutch, which was used in NA Fiesta through its 2019 end and is the weak link (verify by VIN/shifter; web search results were inconclusive on 2018). Later-year revisions improved but did not eliminate problems. Small car with low crash safety margin vs. larger options for 2 kids.
major_issues: DPS6 shudder, slipping, TCM and clutch pack failure 40-120k mi, $1,500-2,500 (clutch/TCM; warranty extended only for 2011-2014 cars); input shaft seal leaks; clutch actuator; Fiesta 1.6 engine mounts, wheel bearings, front suspension; A/C and electrical glitches (SYNC).
risk_reason: If automatic DPS6 at 97k mi: Medium-High risk of clutch/TCM job; if manual, Low. Engine itself low-risk.
inspect_today: Confirm transmission type; on test drive check 5-15 mph shudder, hesitation from stop, rollback on hills, harsh/ delayed shifts, and any trans warning light; look for fluid weeping at bellhousing; scan TCM codes; check clutch pedal feel if manual; inspect engine mounts, CV boots, struts, tires.

verdict: 2016 Focus SE hatch 2.0L GDI. Generation (2012-2018) is notorious for the DPS6 PowerShift dual-clutch (SE 2.0 was usually the 6-speed PowerShift auto), with class action settlement; 2016 improved slightly but still below average. Verify if manual (rare). Poor pick for a kid-hauling, low-repair-budget buyer.
major_issues: DPS6 clutch shudder, slipping, TCM/clutch/ input seal failures 30-120k mi, $1,500-3,500; transmission replacement possible; 2.0L GDI carbon buildup, rear main/oil leaks, engine mounts, motor/trans mounts; electric power steering issues; coolant leaks, A/C; ignition coils.
risk_reason: 143k miles on a DPS6 PowerShift car is well beyond typical clutch life; clutch pack/TCM/ mounts repairs likely exceed $1,000 if automatic.
inspect_today: Confirm transmission; test drive for shudder at 5-20 mph, delayed engagement, slipping, jerky shifts, and warning messages; look for fluid leaks at bell housing and axle seals; scan TCM codes; check engine/trans mounts, power steering, CV axles, oil leaks at rear main, tires.

verdict: 2019 Fusion SE AWD 2.0L EcoBoost with 6-speed auto, final-generation (2013-2020). More solid than Focus; EcoBoost 2.0 is decent, but coolant intrusion risk and PTU/AWD issues are on record. Reasonable cabin size for kids, average reliability.
major_issues: 2.0L EcoBoost: coolant intrusion/ cracked cylinder issues (mostly 2013-2016 and 1.5/1.6L; 2.0 lower risk), turbo/ wastegate and carbon buildup 100k+ $1,500-3,000; AWD PTU/rear differential fluid leaks $800-1,500; 6F35 trans valve body/shift quality issues; water pump/thermostat housing leaks; engine mounts; A/C and infotainment faults.
risk_reason: 118k miles is OK for the engine but turbo/PTU/trans issues begin to appear; AWD adds PTU cost; the typical year has Medium chance of one >$1,000 item.
inspect_today: Check coolant level/color and oil for milky residue; inspect PTU/ rear diff for leaks; trans fluid and shift quality; listen for turbo whine, boost leaks, check for misfire codes; AWD warning lights; look for coolant weeping at thermostat/water pump; brakes, tires, mounts.

verdict: 2019 Acadia SLE1 AWD with 2.5L (LCV) 4-cyl + 9T50? (actually 6-speed 6T45 for 2.5 FWD; AWD gets 9-speed) automatic. Redesigned generation (2017+) lighter and smaller; CR rates 2019 below average, but few catastrophic engine pattern. No clear 2.5L failure pattern found. 100k miles is early for this engine.
major_issues: Transmission shifting complaints/TCM codes (P0716/P0776/P2714), transmission fluid leak recall; infotainment and Bluetooth faults; AWD rear differential/ transfer case fluid service; carbon buildup in direct injection 2.5L; oil consumption reports (less common than 2.4L); water pump and A/C compressor; brakes/ rotors wear; fuel injector issues; stop/start system battery issues.
risk_reason: Newer car at 100k miles with no widespread engine failure pattern; main risks are transmission electronics and AWD service; below-average CR rating keeps it from being negligible.
inspect_today: Scan for trans codes and test shift quality (hesitation, harsh 1-2/ 2-3 shifts, park indicator fault); check fluid leaks at transmission and rear diff; oil level and consumption signs; AWD operation; infotainment/Bluetooth; recall status by VIN; brakes, tires, A/C, stop/start function.

verdict: 2017 Sierra 1500 4WD 5.3L EcoTec3 V8 (L83) with 6-speed 6L80. The L83 engine can last 250k+ but at 196k it is in the wear zone. Known AFM/DFM lifter failures on this engine generation are the main concern.
major_issues: AFM/DFM lifter collapse and cam wear 80-200k mi, $2,500-4,500; excessive oil consumption (piston rings) ; 6L80 transmission shudder/torque converter issues $1,500-4,500; torque-converter shudder (fluid flush 'Mobil 1 ATF' fix); 4WD transfer case / actuator failures $500-1,500; rear brake lines/ rust; front diff / wheel bearings, ball joints; fuel pump; infotainment.
risk_reason: 196k miles: lifter/AFM, 6L80 trans shudder, transfer case and suspension all common and each can exceed $1,000; as-is.
inspect_today: Cold start listen for lifter tick/ misfire; scan for P0300/P0301 and AFM codes; check oil level and blow-by, oil consumption evidence; trans shudder at 40-60 mph, flare; transfer case engagement and leaks; frame and brake line rust; suspension/ball joints; wheel bearings; check records for oil changes.
sources: GM truck owner forums (L83 AFM lifters)

verdict: 2017 Terrain SLE1 AWD 2.4L Ecotec (LEA) with 6-speed. This 2.4L engine has a documented oil consumption defect (piston ring design), class action, and timing chain stretch/failure often triggered by low oil. Even though 2017 had revised parts, owners still report failure. At 167k miles it is a gamble.
major_issues: Excessive oil consumption (1 qt per 1,000 mi or worse) from piston rings; timing chain stretch/P0016 and failure, some at 99k mi; engine replacement $3,500-6,000 (rebuild/ used); PCV system issues; carbon buildup; water pump/coolant leaks; AWD rear diff/PTU; 6T45 trans shifts hard; fuel injectors; A/C.
risk_reason: 167k miles on the known oil-consuming 2.4L with timing chain risk; unknown maintenance; catastrophic engine failure would blow the budget.
inspect_today: Check oil level on dipstick (low or fresh oil is a red flag), look for oil smoke on start/ decel, blow-by, and oil leaks; cold start timing chain rattle; scan for P0016/P0017/P0300 codes; ask for service records; trans shifts; AWD rear diff leaks; coolant condition; check oil cap residue, spark plug oil fouling if possible.
